direct_prompt: In strategic environments characterized by incomplete information, the ability to deceive opponents through bluffing is essential for maximizing long-term utility. title: A Note on the Inapproximability of Correlation Clustering
human_text: We consider inapproximability of the correlation clustering problem definedas follows: Given a graph $G = (V,E)$ where each edge is labeled either "+"(similar) or "-" (dissimilar), correlation clustering seeks to partition thevertices into clusters so that the number of pairs correctly (resp.incorrectly) classified with respect to the labels is maximized (resp.minimized). The two complementary problems are called MaxAgree and MinDisagree,respectively, and have been studied on complete graphs, where every edge islabeled, and general graphs, where some edge might not have been labeled.Natural edge-weighted versions of both problems have been studied as well. LetS-MaxAgree denote the weighted problem where all weights are taken from set S,we show that S-MaxAgree with weights bounded by $O(|V|^{1/2-\delta})$essentially belongs to the same hardness class in the following sense: if thereis a polynomial time algorithm that approximates S-MaxAgree within a factor of$\lambda = O(\log{|V|})$ with high probability, then for any choice of S',S'-MaxAgree can be approximated in polynomial time within a factor of $(\lambda+ \epsilon)$, where $\epsilon > 0$ can be arbitrarily small, with highprobability. A similar statement also holds for $S-MinDisagree. This resultimplies it is hard (assuming $NP \neq RP$) to approximate unweighted MaxAgreewithin a factor of $80/79-\epsilon$, improving upon a previous known factor of$116/115-\epsilon$ by Charikar et. al. \cite{Chari05}.

human_text: A game-theoretic model is proposed to study the cross-layer problem of jointpower and rate control with quality of service (QoS) constraints inmultiple-access networks. direct_prompt: Asteroid deflection represents a critical component of planetary defense against potentially hazardous near-Earth objects (NEOs). The threat of asteroid impacts has motivated extensive research into mitigation strategies. This review examines the primary methods for deflecting asteroids, the optimal locations for intervention, and the necessary timelines for effective action. Kinetic impactors involve deliberately colliding a spacecraft with an asteroid to alter its trajectory via momentum transfer. NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission successfully demonstrated this technique in 2022 by impacting Dimorphos. Gravity tractors utilize the mutual gravitational attraction between a spacecraft and an asteroid to slowly tug it off course. PCA is employed to reduce the dimensionality of measured vibration data, such as frequency response functions, by projecting the inputs onto a lower-dimensional space that captures the principal modes of variation. title: Collective excitations of hard-core Bosons at half filling on square and  triangular lattices: Development of roton minima and collapse of roton gap
human_text: We study ground state properties and excitation spectra for hard-core Bosonson square and triangular lattices, at half filling, using series expansionmethods. Nearest-neighbor repulsion between the Bosons leads to the developmentof short-range density order at the antiferromagnetic wavevector, andsimultaneously a roton minima in the density excitation spectra. On thesquare-lattice, the model maps on to the well studied XXZ model, and the rotongap collapses to zero precisely at the Heisenberg symmetry point, leading tothe well known spectra for the Heisenberg antiferromagnet. On thetriangular-lattice, the collapse of the roton gap signals the onset of thesupersolid phase. Our results suggest that the transition from the superfluidto the supersolid phase maybe weakly first order. We also find several featuresin the density of states, including two-peaks and a sharp discontinuity, whichmaybe observable in experimental realization of such systems.
direct_prompt: We investigate the collective excitation spectra of hard‑core Bosons at half filling on both square and triangular lattices, with particular emphasis on the emergence and evolution of roton minima. Using a combination of linear spin‑wave theory, numerical exact diagonalization, and series expansion techniques, we map out the dispersion relations as a function of interaction strength and lattice geometry. On the square lattice, we find that increasing nearest‑neighbor repulsion leads to the progressive softening of excitations at specific momenta, resulting in well‑defined roton minima in the dynamic structure factor. For the frustrated triangular lattice, the roton features are more pronounced and appear over a broader region of parameter space, reflecting the enhanced role of quantum fluctuations. We demonstrate that upon approaching critical interaction strengths, the roton gap collapses, signaling an instability toward density‑wave or supersolid ordering depending on the lattice and parameter regime.

title: Photo-z for weak lensing tomography from space: the role of optical and  near-IR photometry
human_text: We study in detail the photometric redshift requirements needed fortomographic weak gravitational lensing in order to measure accurately the DarkEnergy equation of state. In particular, we examine how ground-based photometry(u,g,r,i,z,y) can be complemented by space-based near-infrared (IR) photometry(J,H), e.g. on board the planned DUNE satellite. Weconsider a DUNE-like broad optical filter supplemented with ground-basedmulti-band optical data from surveys like the Dark Energy Survey, Pan-STARRSand LSST. We show that the Dark Energy Figure of Merit would improved by afactor of 1.3 to 1.7 if IR filters are added on board DUNE. Furthermore we showthat with IR data catastrophic photo-z outliers can be removed effectively.There is an interplay between the choice of filters, the magnitude limits andthe removal of outliers. We draw attention to the dependence of the results onthe galaxy formation scenarios encoded into the mock galaxies, e.g the galaxyreddening. For example, deep u band data could be as effective as the IR. Wealso find that about $10^5-10^6$ spectroscopic redshifts are needed forcalibration of the full survey.

Ground-based multi-band optical photometry in filters such as u, g, r, i, z, and y provides a baseline for photo-z estimation. The dark energy figure of merit is evaluated for parameters w₀ and wₐ across various filter combinations and depth scenarios. Deep u-band observations from the ground can alternatively mitigate outliers by distinguishing reddened galaxies, though near-IR data proves more robust across magnitude limits.

human_text: If the recent PVLAS results on polarization changes of a linearly polarizedlaser beam passing through a magnetic field are interpreted by an axion-likeparticle, it is almost certain that it is not a standard QCD axion. In the one-waypropagation, interesting phenomena can occur for special configurations ofpolarization where, for instance, transition occurs but light polarization doesnot change. title: On Lagrangian submanifolds in complex hyperquadrics and isoparametric  hypersurfaces in spheres
human_text: The $n$-dimensional complex hyperquadric is a compact complex algebraichypersurface defined by the quadratic equation in the $(n+1)$-dimensionalcomplex projective space, which is isometric to the real Grassmann manifold oforiented 2- planes and is a compact Hermitian symmetric space of rank 2. From this viewpoint we provide a classification theorem of compacthomogeneous Lagrangian submanifolds in complex hyperquadrics by using themoment map technique. Moreover we determine the Hamiltonian stability ofcompact minimal Lagrangian submanifolds embedded in complex hyperquadrics whichare obtained as Gauss images of isoparametric hypersurfaces in spheres with$g(=1,2,3)$ distinct principal curvatures.

We demonstrate that several important classes of Lagrangian submanifolds, including those that are Hamiltonian minimal or H-umbilic, naturally arise from the principal curvature data of these hypersurfaces. We demonstrate that an exponentialspeed-up is sometimes possible, but that some natural graphs allow only alogarithmic speed-up. title: Parametric Learning and Monte Carlo Optimization
human_text: This paper uncovers and explores the close relationship between Monte CarloOptimization of a parametrized integral (MCO), Parametric machine-Learning(PL), and `blackbox' or `oracle'-based optimization (BO). We make fourcontributions. First, we prove that MCO is mathematically identical to a broadclass of PL problems. This identity potentially provides a new applicationdomain for all broadly applicable PL techniques: MCO. Second, we introduceimmediate sampling, a new version of the Probability Collectives (PC) algorithmfor blackbox optimization. Immediate sampling transforms the original BOproblem into an MCO problem. Accordingly, by combining these first twocontributions, we can apply all PL techniques to BO. In our third contributionwe validate this way of improving BO by demonstrating that cross-validation andbagging improve immediate sampling. Finally, conventional MC and MCO proceduresignore the relationship between the sample point locations and the associatedvalues of the integrand; only the values of the integrand at those locationsare considered. We demonstrate that one can exploit the sample locationinformation using PL techniques, for example by forming a fit of the samplelocations to the associated values of the integrand. This provides anadditional way to apply PL techniques to improve MCO.
direct_prompt: Parametric learning provides a principled framework for representing complex stochastic systems through families of parameterized models. In this article, we investigate the interplay between parametric learning and Monte Carlo optimization, focusing on how sampling-based methods can be harnessed to improve parameter estimation and decision-making under uncertainty. We first formalize the problem of optimizing performance criteria defined as expectations with respect to unknown or intractable probability distributions. We then show how parametric models can be trained to approximate these distributions using data generated by Monte Carlo simulations. The resulting learning-optimization loop allows parameters to be updated in a way that directly targets the objective of interest, rather than merely fitting observed data. We analyze convergence properties of this loop under mild regularity conditions and demonstrate how variance reduction techniques can significantly accelerate learning. In particular, we highlight the role of importance sampling, control variates, and adaptive sampling schemes in stabilizing gradient-based updates. We also present a class of stochastic approximation algorithms that naturally arise from this perspective and relate them to existing methods in reinforcement learning and Bayesian computation.

title: Vector mesons from AdS/TC to the LHC

We perform a spatially resolved spectral analysis andrecover the density, temperature and pressure profiles of the ICM, just relyingon the spherical symmetry of the cluster and the hydrostatic equilibriumhypothesis. We observe that the correlations among X-ray quantities only are inagreement with previous results obtained for samples of high-z X-ray luminousgalaxy clusters. On the relations involving SZ quantities, we obtain that theycorrelate with the gas temperature with a logarithmic slope significantlylarger than the predicted value from the self-similar model. The measuredscatter indicates, however, that the central Compton parameter y_0 is a proxyof the gas temperature at the same level of other X-ray quantities likeluminosity. Our results on the X-ray and SZ scaling relations show a tensionbetween the quantities more related to the global energy of the system (e.g.gas temperature, gravitating mass) and the indicators of the structure of theICM (e.g. gas density profile, central Compton parameter y_0), showing the mostsignificant deviations from the values of the slope predicted from theself-similar model in the L-T, L-M_{tot}, M_{gas}-T, y_0-T relations. title: Quantum spin liquid states in the two dimensional kagome  antiferromagnets, ZnxCu4-x(OD)6Cl2
human_text: A three-dimensional system of interacting spins typically develops staticlong-range order when it is cooled. If the spins are quantum (S = 1/2),however, novel quantum paramagnetic states may appear. The most highly soughtstate among them is the resonating valence bond (RVB) state in which every pairof neighboring quantum spins form entangled spin singlets (valence bonds) andthe singlets are quantum mechanically resonating amongst all the possiblehighly degenerate pairing states. Here we provide experimental evidence forsuch quantum paramagnetic states existing in frustrated antiferromagnets,ZnxCu4-x(OD)6Cl2, where the S = 1/2 magnetic Cu2+ moments form layers of atwo-dimensional kagome lattice. We find that in Cu4(OD)6Cl2, where distortedkagome planes are weakly coupled to each other, a dispersionless excitationmode appears in the magnetic excitation spectrum below ~ 20 K, whosecharacteristics resemble those of quantum spin singlets in a solid state, knownas a valence bond solid (VBS), that breaks translational symmetry. Dopingnonmagnetic Zn2+ ions reduces the distortion of the kagome lattice, and weakensthe interplane coupling but also dilutes the magnetic occupancy of the kagomelattice. The VBS state is suppressed and for ZnCu3(OD)6Cl2 where the kagomeplanes are undistorted and 90% occupied by the Cu2+ ions, the low energy spinfluctuations in the spin liquid phase become featureless.
direct_prompt: A three-dimensional system of interacting spins typically develops long-range magnetic order upon cooling, but quantum fluctuations in S=1/2 systems can lead to novel paramagnetic ground states. Among these, the resonating-valence-bond state represents a highly sought-after quantum spin liquid (QSL), characterized by entangled spin singlets resonating across degenerate configurations. The two-dimensional kagome lattice of corner-sharing triangles is theoretically predicted to host such QSL states due to strong geometric frustration in antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models. The family of compounds ZnxCu4-x(OD)6Cl2 provides experimental realizations of nearly ideal S=1/2 kagome antiferromagnets, with Cu2+ ions forming weakly coupled kagome layers and Zn2+ substitution tuning lattice distortion and magnetic dilution. Elastic and inelastic neutron scattering studies reveal that at low Zn doping, distorted kagome planes exhibit valence-bond-solid-like dispersionless excitations below ~20 K. Increasing Zn content reduces distortion and interplane coupling, suppressing the valence-bond-solid phase. For near-perfect kagome occupancy in ZnCu3(OD)6Cl2, low-energy spin fluctuations become continuum-like and featureless, indicative of a quantum spin liquid ground state with fractionalized excitations and no static order down to the lowest temperatures.

direct_prompt: In this study, we investigate the balance of forces that governs the structural and dynamical properties of simulated lipid bilayers. human_text: Room temperature ferromagnetism is observed in undoped TiO2 films depositedon Si substrates using pulsed laser deposition (PLD). direct_prompt: This study investigates the emergence of ferromagnetism in undoped titanium dioxide (TiO2) arising from intrinsic oxygen vacancies. Utilizing a combination of controlled annealing processes and vacuum treatments, we systematically induced and characterized vacancy concentrations within TiO2 thin films. Magnetic measurements reveal a clear correlation between the density of oxygen vacancies and the magnitude of ferromagnetic ordering at room temperature. The modulation in total viscousdissipation on the superhump period is overwhelmingly from the region of thedisc within the 3:1 resonance radius. direct_prompt: We present a suite of three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations designed to investigate the origin, structure, and evolution of superhumps in accretion discs of cataclysmic variable systems. The simulations employ a high-resolution, grid-based code with an isothermal equation of state, including full tidal forces from a Roche-lobe filling secondary. We systematically explore a wide range of mass ratios, disc viscosities, and mass-transfer rates to identify the conditions under which superhump modulations are excited and sustained. Our results confirm that superhumps are associated with the growth of an eccentric, precessing disc mode excited near the 3:1 outer Lindblad resonance. We demonstrate that the precession rate and superhump period excess correlate strongly with the mass ratio and disc radius, in good agreement with observational constraints. The simulations reproduce both positive and negative superhumps by varying the disc tilt and vertical structure. We find that the amplitude and stability of superhumps depend sensitively on the adopted viscosity prescription and the strength of tidal torques. Disc eccentricity exhibits quasi-periodic cycles of growth and damping, naturally producing the observed evolution of superhump amplitudes over a superoutburst. Synthetic light curves derived from the simulations match the observed morphology of superhump waveforms, including their characteristic asymmetry and harmonic content. Our parameter survey constrains the region of mass ratio and disc size space in which persistent superhumps can exist. We discuss the implications of our results for using superhumps as probes of binary parameters, particularly mass ratios in faint or distant systems. Finally, we outline how these comprehensive simulations can guide future observational campaigns and inform more realistic models including magnetic fields and.

In the dipolespin-down formalism, the 2-sigma upper limit on period derivative implies anenergy loss rate < 1.5E32 ergs/s, surface magnetic field strength B_p < 3.5E11G, and characteristic age tau > 24 Myr.
